story.title: Voice Actor Peter Cullen, Known for Eeyore and Optimus Prime, Passes Away at 85
story.summary: Peter Cullen, the Canadian voice actor celebrated for his roles as Eeyore in Winnie the Pooh and Optimus Prime in the Transformers franchise, has died at the age of 85. His family and agent confirmed his passing, which occurred at his home in Los Angeles.

explore_lenses.label: Why does Cullen’s death resonate so widely?
explore_lenses.title: A voice that connected generations
explore_lenses.summary: Cullen’s best-known characters reached audiences through long-running children’s television, films, toys and fan events. His work as Optimus Prime continued from the 1984 animated series into live-action films through 2023, while his Eeyore performances spanned multiple Disney projects.

claims.text: Cullen voiced Optimus Prime in the 1984 Transformers series and later returned for several live-action Transformers films, including 2023’s Rise of the Beasts.
His Eeyore work included The New Adventures of Winnie the Pooh, The Book of Pooh, My Friends Tigger & Pooh, and several Pooh films.
Hasbro said Cullen shaped how “millions” understood courage, sacrifice and leadership through Optimus Prime; this is the company’s assessment of his cultural impact.

explore_lenses.label: How did he create Optimus Prime’s character?
explore_lenses.title: Prime was rooted in a family example
explore_lenses.summary: Cullen described drawing on his older brother Larry, a Marine veteran, when he auditioned for Optimus Prime. The family’s public request after his death echoes the values Cullen and Hasbro associated with that performance.

claims.text: Cullen said he modeled Optimus Prime on his older brother Larry, who served in the U.S. Marine Corps during the Vietnam War.
Hasbro says Larry’s advice to be compassionate and “strong enough to be gentle” informed Cullen’s 1984 audition and the character’s leadership style.

Cullen received the Lifetime Achievement honor at the 2023 Children’s & Family Emmy Awards, recognizing a career that also included broadcast announcing and many animation roles beyond Transformers and Winnie the Pooh.

story_report.summary: Peter Cullen, the voice actor celebrated for portraying Eeyore and Optimus Prime, has died at 85. His family and agent confirmed that he died at his Los Angeles home on Wednesday, Aug. 26, 2026, surrounded by family. The news ends a career that carried his voice from Winnie the Pooh productions to multiple generations of Transformers, while his family asked admirers to honor him through community service and by leading with compassion, integrity and loyalty.

sections.heading: Peter Cullen’s Defining Voice Roles
sections.body: Cullen first voiced Optimus Prime in the 1984 Transformers series and returned to the role in several live-action films, including 2023’s Rise of the Beasts. His work as Eeyore extended across The New Adventures of Winnie the Pooh, The Book of Pooh, My Friends Tigger & Pooh and several Pooh films. Together, those roles made him closely associated with two enduring animated characters.

sections.heading: Peter Cullen’s Optimus Prime Legacy
sections.body: Cullen said he based Optimus Prime on his older brother Larry, a U.S. Marine Corps veteran of the Vietnam War. Hasbro said Larry’s advice to be compassionate and “strong enough to be gentle” informed Cullen’s 1984 audition and the character’s leadership style; the company also said Cullen shaped millions of people’s understanding of courage, sacrifice and leadership. Cullen received a Lifetime Achievement honor at the 2023 Children’s & Family Emmy Awards for a career that also included broadcast announcing and many other animation roles.

unresolved.text: A cause of death and any public memorial or funeral plans had not been disclosed in the reports reviewed as of Aug. 27, 2026.

related_stories.summary: Catastrophic floods triggered by a glacial collapse near the Nepal-China border have resulted in at least 160 confirmed deaths, with over 1,300 people reported missing. Rescue teams are actively searching for the missing individuals, including a significant number of foreigners. The floods, which swept through communities, were exacerbated by ongoing monsoon rains in the region.

related_stories.summary: Christian Castro, an Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer charged with a nonfatal shooting in Minneapolis, has been released from a Texas jail. A judge denied Minnesota's request for his immediate extradition, leading to his release after an extradition lapse.

related_stories.title: Jury Begins Deliberations in Lindsay Clancy Murder Trial
related_stories.summary: The jury is currently deliberating in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, who is accused of killing her three children. During closing arguments, the defense argued that Clancy was suffering from postpartum psychosis, while prosecutors claimed she intentionally planned the murders. The outcome now rests with the jury.
